title: Set myself a challenge to make a game in under 4 months.
author: FowardJames
selftext:
Been struggling to find communities to share my game, but i've been working hard on this and wanted to share. The demo's live on steam now, let me know your thoughts  
  
[https://store.steampowered.com/app/4605040/Drown\_World/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4605040/Drown_World/)

  
100% vibe coded with Claude Code. Music created with Suno. I bought the tiles from an asset pack, and hand tweaked them. Character and animation made by me. Icons and HUD art made by an artist friend. UI panels made by me. Landmass Art made by ChatGPT

comments.author: RecordingTechnical86
comments.body:
Very nice. How did you make the sprites/graphics? Thats what im struggeling with. 

Also maybe remove the "There are no enemies" in the trailer. It felt like a turnoff. Dont show what you dont have show what you have

replies.author: FowardJames
replies.body:
Fair point about the enemies, its just so many games are combat orientated and I figured it would be a way to stand out. 

Sorry my Post's body got cut off. I updated it but will mention here: the character art was made by me in asesprite. And the Icons/HUD art was from a paid artist. The TileMap was from a pre-bought unity asset pack: [https://assetstore.unity.com/packages/2d/environments/platformer-tileset-pixelart-caves-330017](https://assetstore.unity.com/packages/2d/environments/platformer-tileset-pixelart-caves-330017) 

I took that pack and modified the tile size from 8x8 to 24x24 so my game felt a bit more unique. I also borrowed the asset packs colour palette to inform my characters design. So it felt like it belelonged in the world.

replies.author: FowardJames
replies.body:
I don’t see any Domes  ^_^  did you play the demo btw? For me, it feels like it’s own game. I’m not the first person to take the Dome Keeper core loop and add a spin to it. Check out the game Feed The Deep. 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2332260/Feed_the_Deep/

Certain upgrades like speed, drill damage, carry weight are just unavoidable, I can’t do the core loop without and they’re pretty generic to mining games and games in general. But in the full game. And even in the demo. There’s a lot that sets it apart.

replies.author: IsThisASnakeInMyBoot
replies.body:
Ok I see that game also has a lot of similarities but it's also doing a LOT to separate itself visually. The game I was thinking this looks more similar to tbh was Wall World. I'm going to be 100% honest as a consumer I don't feel like I want to play the demo purely because I've played a lot of Dome Keeper and Wall World 2, so I feel like I've already got a lot of this exact type of gameplay. I'm not saying this as a diss, I love noita too but the influence from noita is FAR less 1:1 than the influence from Dome Keeper.

I can see in your other comments you're not ashamed at all about copying it, which again is fine but I would wager that I'm not the only person who'd be turned away from it because of that. Also I only mentioned the AI angle because I know for a fact there's a ton of gamers that get toxic about AI in games, that's why I would suggest doing a little more heavy lifting to mitigate the copying. No enemies is actually a decent hook, it gives me the feeling that it'd be less stressful than some other games in the genre. You just need to find a few more ways to have your own unique voice.

comments.author: SomeoneYouKnow95
comments.body:
https://preview.redd.it/p9bzlm83z55h1.jpeg?width=2560&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=a6aa897ec7e03ee4230155f89fd2122d72b44dab

Hello op.  
I played and finished your demo in 118 minutes.  
I have to admit last stage with lava rain was quite challenging.  


\>I think of it as Dome Keeper meets Noita  
And that's exactly the same that has popped into my mind instantly OP!  
..And the music giving vibes of risk of rain.

But the mix of everything is well done to not think of it as a ripoff but combined twist.

My issues however are few.  
1) The water damage feels very inconsistent, in just testing few first stages I've caught myself getting a little irritated of popping 2dmg 2dmg whenever I just stood inside a water for a quick moment submerged in half or a tiny bit of water was pouring on me, such a core thing should be adjusted.   
I would have much fun seeing the danger in a form of quick depleting mini-bar above character sprite indicating incoming damage from water than feeling being forced to avoid the water entirely due to its (in my opinion) buggy mechanics.  
It just at moments felt like unfair water boulder dash, and I had to pick armor upgrade just to mitigate it.  
2) The critical sound for depleted fuel is a bit too loud and invasive, alerts are fine, but if it was meant to teach me avoid it completely it surely did.  
3) On 1440p, I was under the impression the main menu had resolution display problems leaning diagonally left down, broken.  
4) I feel like the switching in audiochannels needs more balancing, the drastic switches to left/right is at times very inconsistent and distracting. Very buggy.  
Sometimes it happens all the time and sometimes almost none of the times.  
5) Just a suggestion, after drilling and destroying a square block I feel like these few smaller specks are not enough, depleting them in first stages without active elements, feels a bit empty, perhaps add a tiny gust of dust? What I mean that them disappearing almost instantly feels a bit barebones.  
6) Gamer instincts are the gamer instincts, on the upgrade menu I feel like the ESC button shouldn't bring up pause menu forcing me to press ESC again to return, but act like I used to just to return back from the upgrade menu.   
7) I've found myself not having fun from dropping TNT at first, and then I discovered there's no self-damage from it, I would start doing it earlier if it was well communicated and more encouraging the player to use in tutorial!  
8) While hexagons in upgrade screen icons works visually and are aligned correctly, the ones in the world/stage select looks very bad and need polish, from the whole game they're thing I would accuse of being AI-quality in a bad sense.  
9) The game suffer of the same sin as Noita, single pixel of lava forcing me to take dmg can repel many people off.  
9.5) The whole HP management, It leads often to situations where the player will look at their hp bar and having just one piece of artifact will make them think "Ehhh? Not worth trying anymore, I'd better die or restart".  
I feel like adding a bit more standard hp or single point of shield at start could make it more balanced.  
Anything to not feel like you're dying from something unavoidable. Me personally I don't mind it, but general audience might find it annoying.  
.........Unless it's what you aim for : - )

I really liked little chime sounds whenever drilling through ores, keeps the gameplay very engaging : ) Hud is nice, controls are fluid enough despite blocks sometimes taking one drill instead of two causing accidental breaks.  
I enjoyed your demo, and in later worlds your game have a lot of potential if you make cool twists with new elements.  
For more inspiration perhaps check "powder game"? Super cool old project on simulating material physics, but wouldn't be surprised if you know it already!  
There's really a need for something deeper and unique to avoid people calling it dome keeper clone.

Unfortunately despite my enjoyment, it is rigged with bugs and mechanics acting inconsistent so far, more bug patching and testing IS and WILL be needed before releasing stable 1.0 imo.  
But with the hand on the bible I can say that in these two hours of testing I didn't felt once "This is amateur".  
Wishlisted, I'll remember it, good luck OP.

replies.author: FowardJames
replies.body:
First of all! Thank you for playing the Demo and providing such a high level of Feedback. This feedback is gold.. I started going through each bullet point 1 by 1 on my response, but I basically agree with it all.

There are a lot of quick wins here, the biggest for me is teaching the TNT, I'll likely add a new Hint/Warning on the objective UI at the start of the second/third/4th level to really drill this point in. Because it does change how people play. The audio fixes are also things that I have just overlooked. Super easy to fix. The audio panning is because I am using stereo SFX, so I'll switch them to mono.

I have only tested 1920x1080 and Steam Deck resolutions. So the game likely has issues at other resolutions. Thanks for bringing this to my attention.

Yep the UI in World Select screen is getting re-done, the design was mocked up in Claude. And I did my best to recreate it using Aseprite. But I'm handing over to an artist.

As for the single pixel hurting you. I have made it so if that does happen. The offending pixel should disappear. But it would be a lot better if a single. Lone pixel disconnected from any other for x seconds just disappeared.

Ok, the big one! Water. Right now there are 2 ways water can damage you. The 2HP damage is from fall damage. Which I think is a bit buggy, and I may just remove. The 2nd is drowning damage. If you're fully submerged in water, after a 1 second grace period. You take 5hp damage per second. So originally when I was prototyping. The idea was 'Rain is danger', the world had been corrupted and even standing in rain would start to kill the player. But then I added 20+ liquids to the game. So I think water can just be water now. if I want more threat I can add poisoned water/acid water to the demo's second or 3rd stage.

The full game has 50+ elements (weather, liquids, gases, powders) plus a lot more of the Dwarven tech tree, so there's far more depth coming than the demo shows. And I'll check out Powder Game, thanks for the suggestion.

Once again, thanks for taking the time to play it thoroughly.

replies.author: FowardJames
replies.body:
So I've actually been toying around with your 'mini-bar' idea above the characters head. And I have to say, it feels great. 

I have removed water cascade damage (when it would fall on your head)   
And I have upped the grace period for 'Drown' damage from 1 second to 4 so you can actually react to the bar above your head. 

This way the players can actually risk diving under water to form new paths.   
I've bumped the damage on this from 5 to 18 (full hp is 100) because its pretty easy to avoid drowning now. 

I'm a little worried the first stages of the demo will be to easy now but easy and readible' beats 'challenging andd glitchy'.  

Plus you still have all the usual hazards i.e. Lava

Its completely changed how water deals damage in my game, I'm a bit scared to change it this close to Next Fest, but also excited. So I think its the right call. 

Look out for a demo update in the next few days
